author: Kai Moreno
title: Console session and personal access token revocation
content:
# Purpose
A user can revoke their own Console sessions and personal access tokens (PATs) used for git-style repo access to prompt templates. These are not org API keys.

# When to use
They lost a laptop, saw a Console session they do not recognize, or want to revoke a PAT named after a person. They are not asking about org keys named prod-web or prod-backend.

# Steps
Settings → Security → Sessions → Revoke, or Settings → Personal tokens → Revoke. A PAT revoke does not disable org API keys. An org API key disable does not end Console sessions.

# Priority and routing
How-to is P4, Support. A stolen laptop plus an org API key on that laptop is two jobs: this page for the session, the Hosted API key playbook for the org key.

# Guardrails
Do not disable every org key because someone lost a laptop. Ask which org keys were on the device.

# Related
Console security settings. Hosted API key playbook for org keys only.
